clue.text: Joe outlined arm movement in love play

definitions.note: a play whose subject is love: Shakespeare's tragedy of young lovers

indicators.note: movement means the letters of the three words are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer traces a gesture with an arm during a romantic stage piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' signals rearranging JOE, OUTLINED and ARM; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of two star-crossed teenage lovers is the most famous romance in drama.

clue.text: Hoarsely loud, caucus rhyme

explanation.surface: A political meeting described as noisy, with a poet's note on rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, strident voice is raucous; and the word chimes with caucus, a party meeting, in its ending sounds.

clue.text: MD putting out court disclaimer

indicators.note: putting out suggests the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor issues a formal disclaimer to a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: MD looks like Doctor of Medicine; here it is the abbreviation for the person who conducts a show's orchestra. 'putting out' rearranges COURT DISCLAIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: MD is the standard abbreviation for the conductor in charge of a theatre's music.

clue.text: Duck-eggs perhaps, long seen in cricket ground

parts.note: duck eggs are, like all eggs, ova

explanation.surface: Duck eggs and a long stay are things you might see at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'duck' is a score of nought, which tempts you towards O; here duck eggs are simply eggs. THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington, south London, is a famous Test cricket venue.

clue.text: Central pair leave the swimming race

indicators.note: the two letters in the very middle of the word for swimming are dropped out of it

parts.note: natation is a formal word for the act or art of swimming

explanation.surface: In a swimming race, the two middle competitors drop out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central pair leave' removes AT, the middle two of the eight letters of NATATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people of shared descent is a nation.

clue.text: Jack not finishing piano version of Camellia

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged
the word Jack is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A man named Jack plays an unfinished piano arrangement of a piece called Camellia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts Jack to JAC; 'version of' then rearranges JAC with PIANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Camellia japonica is the common garden camellia, often just called by its species name.

clue.text: Sell iodine extract for protection of bats

indicators.note: to extract is to draw out, so the letters are pulled about and reordered

explanation.surface: A salesman pushing an iodine extract as a remedy for bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' suggests flying animals, but these are cricket bats, treated with oil to protect the willow. 'extract' rearranges SELL IODINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are traditionally rubbed with flax-seed oil to seal and preserve the wood.

clue.text: One showing stress at end of sentence

definitions.text: One showing stress at end of sentence

parts.words: One showing stress at end of sentence
parts.note: reads like a prisoner anxious at the close of a jail term, but means the punctuation that shows emphasis at the close of a written sentence

explanation.surface: A convict shows signs of strain as their prison term draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol placed after an emphatic or excited sentence indicates strong feeling.

clue.text: Standard disciple of parish priest

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a son can mean a disciple or spiritual follower

explanation.surface: A model follower of the local vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman with charge of a parish, especially in the Church of England, is commonly so called.

clue.text: Social climber at university receives shock

parts.note: up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford
a start is a sudden jolt of surprise

explanation.surface: An ambitious student gets a nasty surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has risen suddenly in rank and behaves arrogantly is a jumped-up newcomer.

clue.text: A canapé prepared as a cure-all

indicators.note: food prepared is made up, so the letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A party snack is served up as a remedy for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges A plus CANAPE (the accent is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy claimed to fix every ill is a universal medicine.

clue.text: This is not repeated in a concerto

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words a concerto

explanation.surface: A musical direction warning that a passage in a concerto is played only one time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' shows the answer is tucked inside 'a concerto'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens a single time, never again, happens just the one time.

clue.text: Parts of pub serving loaf-sticks?

parts.note: to loaf about is to lounge idly
bars are rods or sticks

explanation.surface: A pub offering bread sticks with its drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf-sticks' looks like bread; the two halves are a verb (idle) and a noun (rods).
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional British pubs had separate rooms, the more comfortable ones being lounges as distinct from the public bar.

clue.text: Cooked pies intact, germ free

indicators.note: cooked suggests fiddled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pies baked whole come out hygienic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges PIES INTACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sterile substance that kills microbes is described by this word.

clue.text: Fish not taken originally in British water

parts.note: sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the words not and taken

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in British seas that nobody has caught yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of 'not taken'. THE SOLENT is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England.
explanation.definitionFit: The strait separating the Isle of Wight from Hampshire is a well-known British channel.

clue.text: Sharp drops in pollution

parts.note: acid means sharp or sour in taste
rain falls as drops of water

explanation.surface: Sudden falls in pollution levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' reads as decreases; it is falling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation made acidic by sulphur and nitrogen emissions is a well-known form of environmental damage.

clue.text: From Parma, it's smoked beef

indicators.note: smoked suggests the letters have been cured and transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: A deli boasts its cured meat comes from Parma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoked' rearranges PARMA and ITS (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned, smoked cut of brisket is a deli favourite.

clue.text: Turkish blade swings it, I scram!

indicators.note: swings means the letters are swung around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone flees as a swordsman flourishes a curved sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swings' rearranges IT, I and SCRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved oriental sabre is the weapon associated with Turkish and Persian warriors.

clue.text: Flexible composer accepts lire

indicators.note: accepts means the composer's name takes the money inside it

parts.note: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of light operas
L is the abbreviation for the Italian lira, plural lire

explanation.surface: An accommodating composer happily takes payment in Italian money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts L inside SUPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliant and bending easily is described with this word.

clue.text: Note area of smallest possible numbers

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A remark about the region with the lowest figures.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the lowest values a function reaches are its least values, plural of the Latin term.

clue.text: No bread for him in his game

definitions.text: No bread for him in his game

parts.words: No bread for him in his game
parts.note: bread is slang for money: a player who earns nothing from the sport he plays

explanation.surface: A hungry sportsman finds no food on offer at his match.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsperson who plays unpaid, for love rather than money, is a non-professional.

clue.text: Ancient old boy putting up wine-shop

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means the letters are written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: aged means very old
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An elderly former pupil is setting up a wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' reverses AGEDOB, giving the Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish-speaking countries a small shop or cellar selling wine is so named.

clue.text: Anticipation of preferred alternative healing

explanation.surface: The saying that heading off illness is better than treating it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition alludes to the proverb that it is better than cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipation in its old sense means forestalling; and stopping an illness beforehand is the proverbial preferable option to curing it.

clue.text: Small coin of Indian nation

indicators.note: of shows the answer is made from letters inside the words Indian nation

explanation.surface: A minor piece of currency from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to letters tucked across 'Indian nation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Indian currency unit worth one sixteenth of a rupee was a small coin.

clue.text: Had Jerusalem first in mind as destination for pilgrimage

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A traveller planned on Jerusalem as the goal of a holy journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes J from Jerusalem. The answer's real destination is Mecca, not Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, an obligation of faith, has this alternative spelling.

clue.text: Girl, given new title, gets first-class return

indicators.note: new means the letters of the word title are made new, rearranged
return means the letters for first-class are read backwards

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A woman with a newly granted title enjoys a top-notch reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TITLE as LETIT; 'return' reverses AI (A1) to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, a variant of Latin Laetitia meaning joy.

clue.text: Issue English chap devoured

parts.note: a chap is a man
devoured means ate

explanation.surface: The problem is that an Englishman got eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning flow out.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow out or proceed from a source is the verbal sense of issue.

clue.text: In theory, he is no prankster

definitions.text: In theory, he is no prankster

parts.words: In theory, he is no prankster
parts.note: a playful contradiction: someone of theory is hardly practical, and a prankster is anything but serious, so the words pair opposites

explanation.surface: A theorist insists that he never plays tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoaxer who plays tricks with real effects on victims is a prankster of a hands-on kind.
